column2: A GPU cloud gets its hardware months before its first customer.
Nordhaven is a fictional NVIDIA Cloud Partner: inference in Paris, training in Finland.
Inside, training and post-training run east-west, GPU to GPU. On the Finland node, I measured 351 gigabytes per second over NVLink.
Inference runs north-south. Requests come in, tokens go out. I designed that layer with NVIDIA Dynamo, and it runs next.
Between handover and the first tenant, every partner asks the same four questions.
AICR pins the versions that go together. NVCRE certifies each node before any tenant lands on it.
When a GPU fails, NVSentinel had training back in 288.8 seconds, with nobody involved. My own controller from Part 1 took 360.9.
KAI and MIG share scarce GPUs between teams. Slurm users and VM customers run on the same platform.
Thanos gives one view of both sites, even after one of them is gone.
All of it runs on upstream Kubernetes, from one Git repository, across two providers.
From hardware handover to first tenants, on NVIDIA's open stack. That's the work I can do for a partner.
